questions.text: Compared with a Q-Former bottleneck, what is the main token-budget tradeoff of projecting every image patch through an MLP?

options.A: It produces a single pooled token but requires training both encoders.
options.B: It removes visual tokens from the context but requires gated LLM layers.
options.C: It preserves one token per patch but uses more LLM context positions.
options.D: It fixes the output at 32 tokens but requires extra contrastive losses.

questions.explanation: A per-patch MLP changes embedding width without reducing patch count. This avoids a fixed-query bottleneck but consumes more context positions.

questions.text: During LLaVA stage-1 projector alignment, which components are trained using caption language-modeling loss?

options.A: Only the projector, while the vision encoder and LLM stay frozen.
options.B: Only the vision encoder, while the projector and LLM stay frozen.
options.C: Only the LLM, while the vision encoder and projector stay frozen.
options.D: The vision encoder and LLM, while the projector stays frozen.

questions.explanation: Stage 1 learns the projector mapping using a frozen vision encoder and frozen LLM, with caption LM loss.

questions.text: In the toy code, what does build_llava_prompt(system, user, image_tokens=576) actually do with the image placeholder?

options.A: It replaces the placeholder with 576 numeric embedding vectors.
options.B: It keeps the placeholder in raw_prompt and records the count as metadata.
options.C: It runs the vision encoder and inserts 576 generated text tokens.
options.D: It removes the placeholder and verifies the LLM context length.

questions.explanation: The helper builds a string containing <image> and returns the supplied image_tokens count separately. It does not implement embedding insertion or model execution.
